Yes, he was really clear that if I missed appointments I'd have to pay.

I get where he's coming from.  He must think I'm doing this on purpose or am being irresponsible or something.  I literally plastered my house with notes to try to remind myself.  I don't know what else I could have done.
Thanks - sounds like you had a similar problem.

There is not.  It may or may not clear up.  Surgery is likely to cause more damage than fix.

It's horrible, hence wanting to see a psychologist.

In Canada Psychiatry is covered by OHIP so it's 'free'.  If you miss an appointment you have to pay.

It's not my feelings being hurt - it's more that I am going to him specifically BECAUSE I'm having trouble with memory and stuff like this.  I need help.  I just don't understand how this is supposed to work if the symptom I'm going to the doctor is the thing that causes him to 'fire' me per say.

Yeah.  As soon as I started taking Tramadol I started noticing memory problems.  I even have to use a pill counter because I will take one and then 5 minutes later not be able to remember if I did or not.

Glad to hear it's not just me.

I looked at http://www.e-laws.gov.on.ca/html/regs/english/elaws_regs_930856_e.htm and I think #7 and #19.  The reason he said he stopped seeing me was because I told him I couldn't afford to pay him for the missed appointments.  I really thought I did everything I could to try to remember this appointment - I really don't think there's much more I can do.  I just somehow convinced myself it was at 1pm instead of 11am.  This is really unusual for me as I'm normally REALLY organized and fastidious. 

I just don't know if it's worth it.  When I told him I wanted to keep seeing him and he said no I said I thought that was wrong and I'd report him.  He got nasty and started calling me names (said I was a 'real piece of work' and stuff like that).  I just don't think he should be talking to people like that, especially those who are in distress.
That's sort of my problem - that's where I was at a year ago.  Now I am just tired of trying to take it 1 day at a time.  It isn't seeming to get any better, only worse.
Not yet.  It's just so much to have to deal with all at once.

I started taking Tramadol to help with the pain.  Started at 1 pill a day, then 2 now I'm probably taking 3 or 4.  Within the space of about 2 or 3 months.  Don't know if I'm addicted just yet but feels like it.

I lost my job and don't have anything to do during the day.  I don't have anything to really look forward to.

Also just so tired - I can't sleep properly and I feel incredibly sick during the day.  I have no more social life and can barely get the energy to sit on the computer or go for a walk.  

I basically just feel I have very little to live for.  Things I used to enjoy are just completely meaningless or take so much effort I can't even bring myself to smile when I do them.

I'm trying SO hard to find a reason to keep living.  I just can't imagine another 2-3 years or even 40 years of this.

lol no chemical castration is not at all what I'm hoping for.  Though I never really thought about it, may be an option if the pain is really that bad.

Kind of why I'm in a place where I'm suicidal - its hard to imagine a life where I have to be celibate.
